input.title: Verify in production: the operator console is published and reads the live Worker
input.body:
The console merged in #85. Its behaviour is proven by CI — 17 screen goldens, and server cases against the real Worker — but **being published is not**: GitHub Pages is not enabled yet (#86), so nothing has ever built and served this artifact, and no run has read a live corpus.

The two things CI cannot see are the two that only exist once it is live: that the Pages workflow actually publishes, and that a browser on the open internet can reach the Worker's `/api/v1/status` across origins — the console is on `github.io` and the API is not, so this is the first cross-origin read the API has ever served in anger.

```
Original-issue: #81
In-production-when: https://missingbulb.github.io/hitbut/ answers 200 with HTML containing "operator"
Verify: that page's JavaScript reaches the API — fetch the Worker's /api/v1/status directly and confirm 200 with a JSON body carrying a `totals` object and an `access-control-allow-origin` header; then confirm /api/v1/operations answers 401 or 503 rather than 200, because an operations route that answers an uncredentialled request is the one failure that matters here
Not-before: 2026-08-30T00:00:00Z
Retry-every: 3 days
```

Model: sonnet

**Instructions to the run.** You are executing this, not deciding it.

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real URL. Never infer it from a merge or from elapsed time. A 404 means Pages is still off — that is the normal state until #86 is done.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the evidence you actually read — the status code, the CORS header value, and the totals — and close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen #81 with a comment saying what was asserted, what happened instead and the URL you read it from; comment here linking that; close this issue as completed, because the verification did its job by finding the fault.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by 3 days, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

Note the ordering: `/api/v1/status` needs a live Worker, which is #27's, and the page needs Pages, which is #86's. Either being incomplete shows up as step 1 or step 2 failing, and both are expected for now.

Refs #86, #27

{"id":5226784560,"number":81,"state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","locked":false,"title":"An operator dashboard: what the corpus holds and what the crawl did","body":"There is no way to look at the running product and see what it holds or what it last did. The public API answers questions about *one* figure or *one* finding; nothing answers "how much is in here, is the crawl working, what broke".

**Scope, decided with the owner:** the corpus and the operations only. Nothing about visitors — no search-term logging, no share counters, no client error beacon. Those would each need a write surface (which `5.8` refuses) and a retained record of what a reader typed, and a product whose roster note says *we do not track personal activity* should not start with its own readers. The dashboard answers from what the server already knows about itself.

## What it shows

- **The corpus**: figures, utterances, attestations, clusters, findings — counts, plus the distribution of utterances over venue and over year, and how many carry no date at all.
- **The crawl**: per source module, when it last ran, what it fetched, what came from cache, what failed and why. A module that has **never** run reads as never-run, not as zero — the difference is the whole point of looking.
- **Server-side failures**: the reasons a run recorded, which are already produced by acquisition and the ingestion pipeline and today are thrown away when the scheduled handler returns.

## Two routes, split by what the data actually is

- `GET /api/v1/status` — **public**. Corpus counts and distributions. Every number in it is already derivable from the public corpus API by walking it, so gating it would be theatre.
- `GET /api/v1/operations` — **credentialled**. Runs and failure reasons. Failure text names internals, so this half is not public.

## Auth

A static page cannot hold a secret, so the credential is supplied by whoever is looking: a bearer token compared against a Worker secret, kept in the browser. Unset secret means the route answers "not configured" rather than answering openly — it fails closed and says which.

The alternative worth recording is **Cloudflare Access** in front of the route: it runs the login itself and sets a long-lived HttpOnly cookie, which is the shape the owner asked about. It is not implemented here, because an Access-aware branch has to trust a forwarded identity header, and a branch that trusts a header is a privilege escalation the moment the route is not actually behind Access — and there is no account here to exercise it against (#27). It goes in `DESIGN.md` as the deployment alternative, unexercised and marked so.

## Where it lives

Its own app under `src/dashboard/`, published to GitHub Pages, separate from the product site — the site is a public Hebrew reading surface and this is an English operator tool. The barrier rules gain a third party so the dashboard cannot reach into the backend either.

## Requirements

A new section in `dev/requirements/requirements.md` rather than a second spec file. The harness resolves exactly one `SPEC_PATH` and one requirements root, and the coverage bijection is one leaf ↔ one case across all kinds — a second spec would mean a second gate, a second registry and a second set of runners for requirements about the same product. Section 8, new ids, existing kinds.

Blocked on nothing: it is built and proven against the same fake world as everything else, and lights up with real numbers when #27 lands.

Comment class: feature Two decisions, then a console. You picked corpus-and-operations only, which is the version that needed no write surface and no change to what the product keeps about anybody. **Your Cloudflare login question — the honest answer is that it authenticates against the wrong system.** The dashboard's numbers live in *our* D1, reachable only through our Worker; a Cloudflare token, read-only or not, would not fetch a corpus count, and it is account-scoped — far more authority than showing totals needs. The flow you described does exist, as **Cloudflare Access**: it runs the login and leaves a long-lived HttpOnly cookie, no token in JavaScript. Two things stop it being today's answer. Its cookie belongs to the hostname it protects and its login is a redirect a `fetch` cannot follow, so the console would have to leave GitHub Pages for a Cloudflare hostname. And an Access-aware branch must trust a forwarded identity header — a privilege escalation the moment the route isn't actually behind Access. I did not write it. It's in [`DESIGN.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/main/docs/architecture/DESIGN.md) as the alternative, marked unexercised. I also couldn't check Cloudflare's own specifics: the sandbox gateway refuses `api.cloudflare.com` at CONNECT, a policy denial confirmed in the proxy's own status. **And a different file — no.** The harness resolves exactly one `SPEC_PATH` and one requirements root, and the bijection is one leaf ↔ one case *across all kinds*. A second spec means a second gate, a second registry and a second set of runners, for requirements about the same product. § 8, nine new leaves, existing kinds. [PR #85](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/85), merged as `3070869`.
**`src/dashboard/`** — new. The console: stat tiles, two distributions, the source table, the token panel. **`src/backend/corpus/`** — `0008` gives the crawl a run log; totals and distributions. **`src/backend/api/`** — `/status` public, `/operations` credentialled and failing closed. **`src/backend/`** — the scheduled pass records what it did instead of dropping it. **`src/shared/`** — the wire types for both routes. **`.github/workflows/`** — publishes the console to Pages. **`docs/architecture/`** — why the routes split where they do, and the Access alternative.
Three things the tests caught that I would not have: - **`8.3` did not catch a weak comparison.** I made `sameSecret` accept a prefix and the case stayed green — it tested a longer token and a same-length wrong one, never a strict prefix, which is exactly what a compare that stops at the first difference lets through. Fixed, and it reddens now. - **The screen lane found a determinism defect in my own page.** The masthead printed the *server's* wall clock, so three goldens drifted every run. It reads this device's clock now — which is what "how fresh is this screen" actually asks — while the server's `readAt` stays on the wire, where staleness is measured against it. Byte-identical on a CI runner afterwards. - **The palette validator rejected my first status colours.** Grey and oxide came out at ΔE 14.9 for normal vision — below the floor, and they were "never run" and "failing", the two states this page exists to tell apart. Never-run now draws no status colour at all: it is the absence of a reading, not a fourth state, and every one of its cells is a dash rather than a zero. Also worth knowing: **the queue is busy again.** Since Actions came back, other sessions have merged provisioning work — #27's checklist became a workflow, and a D1 id is pinned. I merged `main` into this branch and resolved one `package.json` conflict, keeping both sides. > ⚠️ Still open: [#86](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/86) **turn on Pages** — Settings → Pages → Source: GitHub Actions; nothing publishes until you do · [#87](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/87) the verification that comes back on its own once it's live · [#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27) Cloudflare provisioning, now partly automated by another session · `wrangler secret put DASHBOARD_TOKEN` for the operations half · **the real roster**, still yours

Every resource the account needs is one non-interactive `wrangler … create`,
and both deploy origins are readable off the deploys themselves — so neither
the per-resource dashboard clicking nor the two-pass first deploy was ever
necessary. A `provision` workflow now creates whatever the preflight reports
missing, reads the D1 id back and commits it; the deploy reads each origin
back and hands it to the next step.

The runner is closed by default — it lists, it creates, it deploys — so no

name: ship main
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: [checks, screen]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
      CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Is there an account to deploy to yet?
        id: account
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ]; then
            echo "Cloudflare provisioning (issue #27) has not landed — nothing to deploy yet."
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm ci
      # Turns "the deploy failed somewhere in wrangler" into a named missing resource.
      # Everything it can report missing is one run of the *provision* workflow away.
      - name: Does production exist?
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run preflight
      - name: Bring the corpus schema up to date
        if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'
        run: npm run corpus:migrate:remote
      # Each deploy step reads its origin back and exports it, so the site is built against
      # the API that was just deployed and the smoke test knows where to look. A repository

Comment class: other

**#69's deploy path has now run against the real account twice, and both runs are red. `main` is red with them.** Here is what preflight actually read, from [run 49](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/actions/runs/32639537816) on `3070869`:

```
[ok  ] secret CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID        set (32 characters)
[ok  ] secret CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN         set (53 characters)
[ok  ] wrangler.toml database_id           pinned to 2a7f04e1-…
[ok  ] D1 database hitbut-corpus           found
[??  ] R2 bucket hitbut-raw                `wrangler r2 bucket list` failed —
                                           a request to /accounts/…/r2/buckets failed
[ok  ] Pages project hitbut                found
[MISS] Vectorize index hitbut-utterances   not in the list
```

So most of it worked. The account is real, the token authenticates, D1 and Pages are there and the id is pinned. **One thing is not merely missing — it is unanswerable.** The R2 listing failed rather than coming back empty, which is exactly the distinction preflight was built to draw, and it is why the provisioner will not create the bucket: it refuses to create on an unanswered question.

**Two candidate causes, and I cannot tell them apart from here.** Either the API token has no R2 permission (`Workers R2 Storage`), or R2 is not enabled on the account at all — of the products on this list it is the one that needs a separate activation with billing details before its API answers. Cloudflare's docs are unreachable from this sandbox (the gateway refuses `developers.cloudflare.com` and `api.cloudflare.com` at CONNECT), so that second half is reasoning from the shape of the failure, not something I read. Whoever holds the dashboard can settle it in a minute: if R2 has never been activated, activate it; if it has, re-issue the token with R2 included.

Vectorize is a plain `MISS` and is optional — `npm run provision` creates it once the token can answer.

**The second finding is about the workflow rather than the account.** `ship main` runs `npm run preflight`, which exits 1 on "not ready to deploy" — so **every merge to `main` is red until R2 is answerable**, whatever the merge contained. Before #69 that job skipped cleanly with a message. Red `main` is this project's shipping-outage signal, and it is now permanently on for a reason that is not a shipping problem, which is the fastest way to teach everyone to ignore it.

The smallest fix that keeps what #69 wanted is to distinguish the two states the job currently conflates: *production does not exist yet* — skip the deploy, say so, exit clean, exactly as the `account.ready` gate already does for missing secrets — versus *production exists and something is wrong* — fail loudly. Preflight already knows which it is; the deploy job just needs to read it as a state rather than as a pass/fail. I have not pushed that: it is #69's design, it landed an hour ago, and there is no way to exercise the deploy path from here — so it belongs to whoever owns that workflow rather than to a drive-by patch from the change that happened to merge next.

Nothing in #85 caused either finding. It reproduces identically on `836ec57`, #69's own merge, which is the commit before mine.

Refs #69, #85

[MISS] Vectorize index        (optional)

Either the token has no R2 permission, or R2 was never activated on the account — of that list it's the one product needing separate activation. I can't tell which from here and I've said so on [#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27#issuecomment-5386014134) rather than guessing; Cloudflare's docs are refused at the gateway.

**The second finding is the one I'd act on first.** `ship main` runs preflight, which exits 1 on "not ready to deploy" — so **every merge to `main` is red until R2 answers**, whatever the merge contained. Before #69 that job skipped cleanly. Red `main` is this project's shipping-outage signal, and it's now permanently on for something that isn't a shipping problem.

I did not push a fix. The job conflates two states preflight already distinguishes — *production doesn't exist yet* (skip, say so, exit clean, exactly as the existing secrets gate does) versus *production exists and something broke* (fail loudly). That's a small change, but it's #69's design, it landed an hour ago from another session, and there's no way to exercise the deploy path from here. The proposed patch is on #27 for whoever owns that workflow.

So: the console is merged and green on its own two jobs; `main`'s redness is one Cloudflare setting plus one workflow decision, neither of which is mine to make.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.

Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.

Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.

- map-a-data-source: Reconnaissance on a website you want data from but don't control — locate the real data surface (hydration blob, client API, or markup) and write the findings down before any parser exists. - prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. `|| true`. The preflight is the honest answer to "did it work"; it now decides
the run.

cannot both try to create the same resource.

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)

content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.subject: Preact+Vite RTL frontend + screen goldens (phase 7)
content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

input.title: The console says "404 from /status" when what it means is "nobody told me where the API is"
input.body:
The published console reports:

> Could not read the corpus: **404 from /status**
> Could not read the crawl: **404 from /operations**

That is my defect, and the number is the tell. A 404 is an *answer*. Something served it — and that something is GitHub Pages, answering for a path on its own host.

**What happens.** `VITE_API_ORIGIN` is empty, because the repository variable `API_ORIGIN` is not set — correctly, since no Worker has ever deployed (`ship main` is red on an unanswerable R2, #27). The client falls back to an empty origin, which makes every fetch a **relative** URL, which resolves against `missingbulb.github.io`. Pages has no `/api/v1/status`, so it 404s.

The message that was supposed to cover this — *"could not reach (no API origin configured)"* — sits in the `catch` branch, and a 404 does not throw. So the one case the fallback existed to explain is the one case it cannot explain.

**The fallback is wrong, not just its message.** A relative URL is a guess that the page and the API share an origin. For this console they never do: it is on `github.io` by design and the API is on Cloudflare. A configuration this page cannot function without should be a named, refused state — not something it quietly guesses at and then misreports as the API's fault. Unknown is a state of its own here as everywhere else in this corpus.

**The fix:** when no API origin is configured, do not fetch at all. Say which variable is missing, and say that both halves are blank because of it rather than because the server answered anything.

## A second thing, from the same screenshot

The masthead collapses on a phone — "hitbut" and "operator" break onto two lines, and the timestamp wraps under itself. Every committed golden is 1280 wide, so nothing was watching the width this console actually gets checked at. The site already has a phone-viewport leaf (`6.7`); the console should have one too, so the narrow layout is a picture somebody approved rather than a thing nobody looked at.

Two new leaves under § 8. Neither needs anything from Cloudflare.

  this leaf the narrow layout is the one nobody has ever approved.
  </details>"""

p.write_text(s)
PY

input.title: Refuse to guess where the API is
input.head: claude/hitbut-api-origin
input.body:
The published console said **"404 from /status"**. The number is the tell: a 404 is an *answer*, and the thing answering was GitHub Pages.

With `API_ORIGIN` unset — correctly, since no Worker has deployed — the client fell back to an empty origin, making every fetch a **relative** URL that resolved against `missingbulb.github.io`. The message written for exactly this case, *"could not reach (no API origin configured)"*, lives in the `catch` branch, and a 404 does not throw. So the one case the fallback existed to explain was the one case it could not.

**The fallback was wrong, not just its message.** A relative URL asserts that the page and the API share a host. This console is on Pages and the API is on Cloudflare — they never do, so the guess is always wrong, and its failure arrives looking like the API refusing rather than like a setting nobody filled in. No origin is now a state of its own: nothing is requested at all, and the page names the variable — **once**, at page level, because both halves were blank for one cause and saying it twice reads as two faults.

## And the width it is actually checked at

You checked it on a phone, which is where an operator checks a crawl. Every committed golden was 1280 wide, so nothing was watching. `8.11` fixes that: the masthead stacks instead of breaking mid-wordmark, tiles go two-up, and the six-column table becomes labelled blocks — a table scrolled sideways hides the module name, which is the column every other one is about. Labels come from the cells, so one source spells each of them.

## What this caught on the way

Setting `VITE_API_ORIGIN` for the whole screen lane **moved every section-6 golden**: the site reads the same variable, and its goldens were rendered with it unset. The lane now sets it for exactly one build and clears it around the others. That is also why the console is built **twice** — the origin is fixed at build time, so "nobody set it" is a different artifact rather than a different runtime state, and `8.10` is about that artifact.

`8.10` was watched failing against the code it replaces: restoring the relative-URL fallback reddens it on both assertions — the page asks its own host, and prints a status code where a setting name belongs.

## Verification

`npm test` 95 · `npm run test:server` 16 · `npm run test:screen` 19, run twice consecutively · typecheck clean · `check_the_world.mjs` 0 blocking.

Closes #95

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)
content.description: Shared fetch module (retry/backoff/bot-wall/raw-to-R2), source registry, queue consumer, pairing, judge interface + versioned prompt, behavior cases.

content.subject: HTTP API on the real Worker (phase 6)
content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

{"id":32646374567,"name":"product","display_title":"Refuse to guess where the API is","workflow_id":339572729,"run_number":62,"run_attempt":1,"event":"pull_request","status":"in_progress","head_branch":"claude/hitbut-api-origin","head_sha":"9b6c5f177770b9e6fb73d4632e62a2ec973d34b5","head_commit":{"message":"Refuse to guess where the API is

The published console reported "404 from /status". A 404 is an answer, and the
thing answering was GitHub Pages: with no origin configured the client fell back
to a relative URL, which resolved against the console's own host. The one case
the fallback existed to explain — nobody set the origin — is the one case it
could not, because the message for it sat in a catch branch and a 404 does not
throw.

A relative URL was never right here. This console is on Pages and the API is on
Cloudflare; they never share a host, so the guess is always wrong. No origin is
now a state of its own: nothing is requested, and the page names the variable,
once, rather than twice for one cause.

Also the width it is actually checked at. The masthead stacks instead of
breaking mid-wordmark, tiles go two-up, and the six-column table becomes labelled
blocks — a table scrolled sideways hides the module name, which is the column
every other one is about. The labels come from the cells, so one source spells
each of them.

The screen lane builds the console twice, because the origin is fixed at build
time: "nobody set it" is a different artifact, not a different runtime state.
VITE_API_ORIGIN is set for exactly that one build and cleared around the others
— setting it for all of them changed how the site fetched and moved every
section-6 golden, which is how that was caught.

content.subject: Author dev/requirements/requirements.md (phase 1 spec)
content.description: Numbered leaves for corpus, search, acquisition, analysis, API, site. Spec-only commit, no code alongside (feature-requirements-first).

content.subject: Build the executable-requirements harness + coverage gate
content.description: Kind registry (logic/behavior/server/screen), case discovery, bijection gate, per-kind runners, gallery generator + gate, CI wiring. Watch the gate go red first.

content.subject: Shared contract + corpus store (phases 2-3)
content.description: src/shared types, D1 schema+migrations, ULID/slug ids, Hebrew-aware search indexing, supersede-not-delete invariants, logic cases.

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)
content.description: Shared fetch module (retry/backoff/bot-wall/raw-to-R2), source registry, queue consumer, pairing, judge interface + versioned prompt, behavior cases.

content.subject: HTTP API on the real Worker (phase 6)
content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.subject: Preact+Vite RTL frontend + screen goldens (phase 7)
content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

content.subject: Deploy plumbing + phase 0 hand-over issue (phases 0, 8)
content.description: wrangler config, deploy workflow from main, and the human-only Cloudflare provisioning checklist issue.
content.activeForm: Wiring deploy and filing the provisioning issue
